frontier.hypothesis: The twelve buffer accesses did not all exist as references to ONE pseudo at global_alloc time in the original compile; some reference was created after RA, or the original's flow-time counts differed for a reason not yet identified. This remains the leading explanation and is now the ONLY frontier item with no measured contradiction: s2 (splitting), s2 (live-length inflation), s3 (duplication), s4 (random permutation, two chassis) and s5 (directed permutation plus the index and sub-pointer partitions) are all measured dead, and s5's sub-pointer number shows even a 7-reference reduction of the parameter does not flip the sort.
frontier.mechanism: allocno priority is computed from flow/sched-time counts, but the bytes we compare against are post-reorg. s2 checked reorg's delay-slot duplication (no 0xC($sN)/0x14($sN) sits in a delay slot in the target) and s3 checked cross-jump (it merges nothing here), but no per-insn provenance table has ever been built for the twelve accesses, and reload-generated address reloads have never been enumerated at all.
frontier.next_probe: Forensics modality: dump the full RTL insn stream at flow, sched and global_alloc for the candidate form (cc1 -da plus BB2_SCHED_DEBUG / BB2_XJUMP_DEBUG / BB2_RELOAD_DEBUG on the instrumented tools/gcc-2.7.2/cc1 — NOT build/cc1) and enumerate, insn by insn, every target byte whose reference could have been created after RA, including reload-generated address reloads. Deliverable is a per-insn provenance table for the 12 buffer accesses and the 5 walk accesses, which either finds the slack or proves the counts are pinned end to end. Use tmp/grind/func_80078654/s5/eval.sh's standalone-chassis compile line as the driver — it isolates the function from the rest of text1b_b.c, which makes the RTL dump readable.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is an artefact of having PATCHED an inherited body rather than re-derived the function: a from-scratch reconstruction of func_80078654 from the target bytes may express the buffer or the walk in a partition no incremental edit of the current body can reach.
frontier.mechanism: Every form measured in s1-s5 is a local edit of one inherited body, and s4+s5 now show that neither 89k random mutations nor a directed cross-product over six chosen axes leaves that dataflow neighbourhood — the permuter mutates spellings rather than inventing a different decomposition, and the two hand-built alternative partitions this session (index walk, sub-pointer) both land strictly worse. The priority model says the answer must lie in a different partition, so a re-derivation is the only systematic way to leave the neighbourhood.
frontier.next_probe: Rederive modality — BUT NOTE THE BLOCKER MEASURED THIS SESSION: m2c is NOT installed (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'm2c'; no ~/m2c checkout). Step one is therefore to install decompals/m2c into .venv, or to hand-derive the reconstruction directly from asm/funcs/func_80078654.s. Then write the reconstruction VERBATIM from that output (not from candidate.c), measure it with tmp/grind/func_80078654/s5/eval.sh (allocno table + byte diff in one call), and specifically check whether the reconstruction expresses arg0 with <= 5 RA-time references or expresses the walk with a second induction variable.

frontier.hypothesis: No further permuter campaign on this function has positive expected value; the modality should be considered closed rather than re-dispatched.
frontier.mechanism: Three chassis and two mutation regimes (129,034 iterations) produced zero score-improving finds, and both regimes converged on the SAME equal-score attractor — rewrites that clobber the walk pointer inside the loop, which the permuter's scorer cannot distinguish from a legal respelling. The search therefore spends its budget in a basin that is semantically invalid by construction.
frontier.next_probe: If the driver dispatches permuter again, do NOT re-run a campaign on this chassis family. The only permuter work with any remaining value is a campaign seeded from a RE-DERIVED chassis (frontier item 2) once one exists — i.e. permuter becomes useful again only after rederive produces a genuinely different decomposition to seed it with.
